title: Photosynthesis
seo_title: Photosynthesis Worksheets: Equation, Light Reactions, Calvin Cycle (High School Biology)
standard_text: Use a model to illustrate how photosynthesis transforms light energy into stored chemical energy.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on photosynthesis (NGSS HS-LS1-5): the equation, chloroplasts, light reactions, the Calvin cycle and Elodea data. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2, powered by light in the chloroplast.
body_html:
How to think about it

Light energy → chemical energy (glucose).

6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2

  • Light-dependent reactions (thylakoids): light splits water, releases O2, makes ATP and NADPH.
  • Calvin cycle (stroma): uses ATP and NADPH to turn CO2 into glucose.
  • The rate is limited by light, CO2 and temperature.
Example

How many CO2 molecules make 3 glucose?

6 per glucose

6 × 3

Answer: 18

Example

Lamp moves closer, more bubbles. Why?

More light

Answer: Photosynthesis speeds up.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their mass from soil. It comes from CO2.
  • Thinking the O2 comes from CO2. It comes from water.
  • Thinking plants never do cellular respiration.

faq.q: What is the equation for photosynthesis?
faq.a: 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2, using light energy captured by chlorophyll.
The light-dependent reactions in the thylakoids make ATP, NADPH and O2. The Calvin cycle in the stroma uses them to turn CO2 into glucose.

faq.q: What limits the rate of photosynthesis?
faq.a: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature.
